subject: Edge inference partner residency & transient-data handling evidence request
messages:
From: EdgeLabs Security <sec@edgelabs.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Supply chain evidence request: edge inferencing partners

Hi Irene,

Thanks for taking this — I'm Tom from EdgeLabs security. As part of our procurement/compliance intake for a joint pilot, our compliance team needs a concise mapping of Redwood's third parties that touch ephemeral inference traffic for streaming/edge use cases. Specifically we need:

- A roster of subprocessors (name + primary service) that handle live/ephemeral inference requests (including KV cache vendors, streaming edge execution partners, CDN/edge GPU providers).
- For each: data residency (country), whether data is logged/stored (and retention), and whether keys are customer-managed or Redwood-managed.
- Short statements (1-2 lines) on transient-data handling and how long any request artifacts persist in logs/metrics.
- Any SOC 2 / SIG / CAIQ artifacts you can share, or a short note if not available.

We're on a tight timeline for vendor onboarding and would like a first pass by EOD Friday (2025-08-15). If you can share an initial CSV export and any bundles (even redacted) that will help accelerate our internal review.

Cheers,
Tom Hsu
Security Program Manager
EdgeLabs
attachments: none
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: EdgeLabs Security <sec@edgelabs.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Aug 2025 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Supply chain evidence request: edge inferencing partners

Tom — thanks for the clear ask. I've attached a CSV export (redwood_subprocessors_20250814.csv) that includes our current roster filtered for services that may see ephemeral inference traffic (KV stores, streaming edge runtimes, CDN/egress). High level replies inline below and we'll follow up with a short narrative bundle.

Quick answers up front:
- Data residency: column in attached CSV (country/region per provider).
- Logging/retention: by default most live inference telemetry is sampled and retained for 7 days; KV cache hits are ephemeral and retained for up to 24 hours except when debug logging is enabled via customer opt-in.
- Keys: we support both Redwood-managed keys (default) and customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for Dedicated/Private deployments; the attached CSV marks whether KMS integration is available.

Next steps I propose:
1) I'll assemble a short narrative and redacted SIG answers for the items you called out and share a link by EOD Friday.
2) Ben and Marcus — can you each provide a 2–3 sentence standing statement on (a) KV cache encryption at rest and (b) escalation/access model for oncall engineers who may need to access ephemeral caches for debugging? I will incorporate verbatim into the bundle.

Tom — would a link to a Drive folder work for the bundle (I'll drop a redacted SIG and any SOC2 statements we can share)?

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Head of Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0187
attachments: redwood_subprocessors_20250814.csv
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Aug 2025 10:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: quick bob/ops statements for EdgeLabs bundle

Ben / Marcus — forwarding EdgeLabs ask. Need two short items to drop into the narrative bundle:

A) KV cache encryption & retention (1–2 lines): confirm AES-256 at rest for persisted cache shards, whether cache backend logs request payloads, and standard retention for cache items. If any provider makes cache contents accessible to their oncall, note the controls (just-in-time access, audited logs).

B) Oncall & escalation access model (1–2 lines): who can request access to ephemeral artifacts, approval flow, and where those access events are recorded.

Please send by 14:30 PST so I can include verbatim in the Drive upload. If you prefer to drop comments directly to the doc I'll share link.

Thanks — Irene
From: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@edgelabs.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Aug 2025 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Supply chain evidence request: edge inferencing partners

Irene — appreciate the quick turnaround. We received the CSV and the initial narrative you uploaded to Drive (link below). A few notes from our side:

- The attached bundle (edgelabs_compliance_bundle_v1.zip) contains our vendor intake CAIQ and a short summary of the differences between our edge execution partners and the upstream cloud providers.
- We can confirm that for pilot customers we will not insist on raw payload retention at our edge partner level; most partners agree to a short retention window (<=48h) and sampling for telemetry. We'll include a signed attestation for the pilot.
- One question for the Redwood engineers: does Redwood involve any downstream vendor that performs tokenization or de-identification after inference results are emitted (i.e., post-response transforms that may persist derived artifacts)? If so, could you note which subprocessors are involved or if that occurs in-house only?

We'll keep the Drive link updated and expect to deliver a redacted SIG Q&A by Monday. I attached the bundle for your intake team.

Thanks — Tom
Security Program Manager
EdgeLabs
